mathematical_checks.finding: orderedCaps contains only nonnegative scalar caps and E<=B. boundedRates contains only nonnegative actual rates below their corresponding caps. Neither predicate includes an ordering of the trajectory or the desired comparison. E<=B constrains caps; it does not require every actual b>=e.

For the actual unit-inlet upper solution, g=(1-Y0,Y0-Y1,Y1-Y2) has g0_prime=-A*g0, g1_prime=A*g0-B*g1 and g2_prime=(B-E)*g1-(E+F)*g2. The matrix is exactly[[-A,0,0],[A,-B,0],[0,B-E,-(E+F)]]. Its off-diagonal entries are nonnegative from A>=0 and E<=B. Zero initial Y gives g(0)=(1,0,0), not the zero vector. The source derives these identities from actual component derivatives and derives continuity from the supplied actual trajectory.

upper_gaps_nonneg applies the already proved positive_solution to the real gap system, zero additive source and nonnegative initial gap. upper_order_gaps then derives1-Y0>=0, Y0-Y1>=0, Y1-Y2>=0 and Y0-Y2>=0. No gap positivity, parameter monotonicity or target comparison is supplied as a premise.

The residual components are(A-a)*(1-Y0)+a*(1-u), (B-b)*(Y0-Y1), and(E-e)*(Y0-Y2)+(F-f)*(Y1-Y2). All signs follow from caps, nonnegative actual rates, u<=1 and the derived gaps. The proof does not incorrectly assert componentwise matrix order for parameter-correlated diagonal losses.

differential_comparison is called with the actual fixed matrix(a,b,e,f). For x-Y, the residual gives dx-dY<=M_actual*(x-Y). Both initial states are zero. Actual u may vary with time and satisfies0<=u<=1 at every positive time; all eight rate/cap scalars stay fixed. The conclusion holds for every t>=0 and every coordinate. Actual state ordering or x<=Y is not assumed.

For each C>=0 the caps(C,2C,C,3C) satisfy orderedCaps. The accepted explicit scaledState supplies actual continuity, unit-inlet derivative equation and zero initial state, so the general theorem has a certified nonempty family of instances. C=0 is included without division by C, using the already proved zero scaled trajectory.

scope_limits: For arbitrary nonnegative ordered caps, the theorem takes an actual classical upper-endpoint solution Y as data. It does not prove a general existence theorem for Y for every independent cap tuple.

The given-Y assumptions are actual ODE, continuity and initial conditions, not the desired ordering. Once such Y is supplied, upper_rates_bounded also places its endpoint tuple in the actual rate box, so it can serve as an attainable upper witness. No separate general IsGreatest set is defined here.
E<=B is a sufficient structural condition, not asserted necessary or a complete classification. Equality and zero caps are allowed; strict ordering and strict stability are not required.
Ordering belongs to the chosen upper trajectory. Actual interior-rate trajectories can have b<e or an unsorted state and still be bounded by an ordered-cap upper trajectory.

The model is the fixed three-node feedforward structure inherited from actualMatrix. General caps do not mean arbitrary graph topology, arbitrary dimension, arbitrary matrix intervals or time-varying coefficients.

The actual and upper functions must be continuous on the nonnegative half-line with the displayed derivative at every positive time. No arbitrary measurable-input existence, almost-everywhere solution formulation or physical apparatus certificate is supplied.

The constant-inlet counterexample fixes caps B=1/2 and E=2 when only f varies, so it lacks E<=B. It does not contradict this sufficient condition; embedding its trajectories into a larger ordered-cap box changes the all-upper tuple.
This is mathematical source/evidence review, not a kernel rerun, human document test, expert review or novelty certification.
